new_statements.quote: A puzzling feature of the Peñafiel orthography is the acute accent mark on most final vowels. According to Rendón (1971: 217), Elotepec words of more than one syllable are generally stressed on the penult; accordingly, in such words the accent mark does not show the location of stress. The same conclusion applies to words in which the accent mark is placed on a clitic, such as the deictic <-ré> or the enclitic first person pronouns <-án> and <-ná>. The location of the accent mark coincides with that of stress only in certain types of words, such as monosyllabics, compounds whose final constituents are monosyllabic, and disyllabic words begining with a prefix (see Table 12).
new_statements.citation: Operstein, Natalie. 2021. The Peñafiel Vocabulary from San Juan Elotepec. Linguistic Discovery 17(1): 13-46 (reporting Rendón, Juan José. 1971. Relaciones externas del llamado idioma papabuco. Anales de Antropología 8: 213-231, p. 217).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Per Rendón 1971 as restated by Operstein: words of two or more syllables generally carry stress on the penultimate syllable; enclitics (deictic -ré, 1sg -án/-ná) do not shift stress; a prefix + monosyllabic root disyllable and compounds ending in a monosyllabic member are stressed on the final (root) syllable, which suggests the real generalization is root stress. Language also reported (Rendón 1971: 216) to have four contrastive tones plus a possible neutral tone.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllables; compounds whose final constituent is monosyllabic and disyllabic prefix+root words have final stress; clitics -ré, -án, -ná fall outside the stress count; 'generally' hedges the penult rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (citation forms from the 1880s Peñafiel vocabulary and Rendón's 1970 field data collected near, not in, San Juan Elotepec); clitics excluded from the domain; tone reported as contrastive alongside stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Elotepec Zapotec = the Papabuco variety of San Juan Elotepec, Oaxaca (ISO zte, elot1235), one of three Papabuco languages with Zaniza (zani1235) and Texmelucan (texm1235). Operstein's data are the 1880s Peñafiel questionnaire; Rendón 1971's field data were collected in the vicinity of, not in, San Juan Elotepec (he could not reach the town). Language moribund (2 speakers in 2010 census per Barriga Puente).

sources.note: p. 25 (sec. 4, Table 12): restates Rendón (1971: 217) that Elotepec words of more than one syllable are generally stressed on the penult; the Peñafiel acute accent on final vowels therefore does not mark stress except in monosyllables, compounds with monosyllabic final member, and prefix+root disyllables; clitics (-ré, -án, -ná) outside the stress count; Rendón (1971: 216) reports four contrastive tones and a 'posible tono neutro'. p. 14: the only publications on Elotepec Zapotec are Belmar 1901 and Rendón 1971.
